timeline.event: DuPont chemist Joseph Shivers developed the segmented polyurethane fiber that became LYCRA, according to the brand owner.
Lenders took ownership of The LYCRA Company after its previous owner defaulted, and a new board was announced.
A 2025 review estimated global elastane production at about 1.2 million tonnes in 2022, roughly 1.1% of all fiber.
Textile Exchange reported elastane output of about 1.5 million tonnes, about 1.1% of global fiber production.
The LYCRA Company completed a Chapter 11 restructuring that eliminated more than 1.2 billion dollars of debt.

timeline.event: DuPont's Orlon became the first commercially manufactured acrylic fiber.
A follow-up of 2,559 workers exposed to acrylonitrile in Orlon production between 1944 and 1991 found no excess cancer mortality.
A domestic washing study estimated that a 6 kg load of acrylic fabric could release more than 700,000 fibers.
Acrylic output was about 1.6 million tonnes, about 1.2% of global fiber production.

timeline.event: Charles Cross and Edward Bevan discovered the viscose process in England.
Finnish viscose workers exposed to carbon disulfide showed a 4.7-fold excess of heart-disease deaths, which disappeared after exposures were reduced.
A South Korean viscose factory linked to mass carbon disulfide poisoning in the late 1980s closed.
Canopy launched its CanopyStyle initiative in October to keep ancient and endangered forests out of viscose supply chains.
Four US retailers agreed to pay 1.26 million dollars in FTC civil penalties for labeling rayon textiles as bamboo.
Kohl's and Walmart agreed to pay a total of 5.5 million dollars in FTC civil penalties over bamboo and eco claims for rayon products.
Man-made cellulosic fibers reached about 8.4 million tonnes, about 6% of all fiber, with viscose the dominant type.

timeline.event: Courtaulds petitioned the FTC for a new generic name for its solvent-spun cellulose fiber.
The FTC approved lyocell as a name for fabric content labeling.
Lenzing acquired the Tencel business.
A life cycle assessment of Lenzing fibers ranked Tencel lyocell among the lowest overall impacts of the fibers compared, for that producer's plants.
Lyocell production was about 370,000 tonnes, making it the third most produced man-made cellulosic fiber after viscose and acetate.

timeline.event: Fibers of the modal type were first developed for industrial uses such as tires, conveyor belts and hoses.
A life cycle assessment ranked Lenzing's Austrian-made modal among the lowest-impact fibers it compared, a result specific to that producer.
A review estimated modal production at about 0.2 million tonnes, around 2.8% of regenerated cellulose fiber output.
Aalto University researchers reported respinning modal and viscose waste into lyocell-type fibers with the Ioncell process.
